request.spec: Reject creating an owner whose telephone number is already used by any other owner. Respond with 409.
request.prompt:
Implement the following change to the application so that it fully satisfies
the specification and all existing and new tests pass. Run the test suite and
make it green before finishing.

Reject creating an owner whose telephone number is already used by any other owner. Respond with 409.

agent.result_text:
All 260 tests pass, including the new `Cp03Tests`.

## Summary

Implemented the rule: **reject creating an owner whose telephone number is already used by any other owner, responding 409.**

The endpoint pipeline (`owners.POST.yml`) already had an `EnsureOwnerUnique` step and a 409-handling `OwnerAlreadyExistsException`/handler in place from prior checkpoints, so the change was scoped to the uniqueness logic:

- **`EnsureOwnerUnique.java`** — replaced the old "same last name *and* telephone" check (which only looked up owners via `findByLastName`) with a telephone-only check across **all** owners (`findAll()`). This is what `Cp03Tests` requires, since a duplicate telephone can now appear under any last name.
- **`OwnerAlreadyExistsException.java`** — updated the Javadoc to reflect the telephone-uniqueness rule.
- **`OwnerRestControllerV1Tests.createOwnerSuccess`** — its success payload reused seed owner George Franklin's telephone (`6085551023`), which correctly becomes a 409 under the new rule. Gave it a distinct telephone (`6081234567`) so it still exercises successful creation. The duplicate-conflict test in that file continues to pass unchanged.

The broadened rule still satisfies the earlier checkpoints: byte-identical (cp01) and same-last-name-and-telephone (cp02) duplicates share a telephone, so they remain rejected, while owners with distinct telephones are accepted.

Verified: `Cp01Tests`, `Cp02Tests`, `Cp03Tests` green, and the full suite is **260 passed, 0 failures**.
